body_lead: The Maharashtra government has sanctioned a Rs 260 crore action plan to address human-wildlife conflict, covering AI-powered alert systems, modern control rooms, rescue infrastructure, and rapid response teams across the state, the Hindustan Times reported. The plan was cleared at a meeting of the standing committee of the Maharashtra Wildlife Board, chaired by forest minister Ganesh Naik at Mantralaya on Tuesday (26 May). Senior forest officials and legislators were also present.
